jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.jd: About Nebius : Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D. The role As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability. You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads. Your responsibilities Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends. Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads. Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts. Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token. Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo. Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery. Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture. Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets. Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead. Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets. Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers. Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations. Must-haves Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch. Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference. Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system. A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving. Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost. Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism. Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams. Nice-to-haves Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, or SmoothQuant. Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or related inference acceleration methods. Experience supporting agentic workloads involving tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration. Familiarity with CUDA or Triton; the role does not require kernel engineering to be the candidate’s primary specialization. Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, or KServe. Implementation experience with cache-aware request routing, PDD, or WideEP, including diagnosing communication bottlenecks and load imbalance. Familiarity with GPU communication libraries and interconnects, such as NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, or RoCE. Benefits & Perks: Competitive compensation Career growth and learning opportunities Flexibility and ownership Collaborative and innovative culture Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects International environment and talented teams What's it like to work at Nebius: Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI Equal Op

jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Amazon Leo, Amazon Leo Networking Software
jobs.jd: Amazon Leo is building a low Earth orbit satellite broadband network to deliver fast, affordable connectivity to customers around the world, including those underserved by traditional infrastructure. Operating a live constellation and its ground network at scale means service disruptions are an inevitable reality, and how quickly we detect them, understand them, and prevent them from recurring defines the trust we earn as a connectivity provider. We are seeking a talented Senior Applied Scientist to build the next generation of observability and availability science for the Leo network. Leo already detects outages, notifies affected customers, and restores service. The frontier is prediction and prevention: reasoning over complex network and ground-segment telemetry to autonomously detect anomalies before they reach customers, attribute root cause automatically across a sprawling event surface, and rationalize a large, still-maturing metric set so responders trust what the system tells them. In this role you will work backwards from the needs of customers and operations teams. You will own the scientific direction end to end, partnering closely with network engineers, the Network Operations Center, and the Incident Management team, and the Software and Networking orginization to translate a long-term science vision into concrete research and delivery roadmaps. Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities * Own the observability and availability science end to end, from long-term vision to research roadmap to production delivery, working backwards from the needs of customers, the NOC, and network engineering. * Develop time-series and graph-based models with dynamic baselining that detect network and ground-segment anomalies before they cross the High Severity threshold, enabling proactive investigation rather than reactive response. * Reason over complex, multi-system telemetry to attribute cause automatically during live HSEs and LSEs, so Call Leaders and engineers spend time mitigating, not hunting. * Provide the science behind the network's bucketed availability decomposition (geometric and satellite coverage, ground and network segments, customer terminals, payload, and planning), attributing every movement to a true cause rather than noise, so leadership steers on signal and engineering effort lands where it actually moves availability and throughput. * Deliver the models, analyses, and metrics that feed the daily system readiness and validation review consumed by senior leadership and product and engineering, turning availability and throughput data into a defensible, evidence-based read on progress against GA entry criteria. * Own the recurring, fleet-wide "hot topic" investigations that span ASIC, firmware, payload, network, and planning, separating correlated symptoms from true root cause across thousands of nodes, quantifying how much availability or throughput each is costing, and answering whether it is a launch-blocking risk and whether it is improving. * Deliver alert correlation and deduplication, false-positive reduction, and metric-quality scoring so responders trust what the system tells them, directly supporting a large, still-maturing KPI set. * Tie your science to the unit the org actually measures: reduce detection and attribution time, raise availability against the network's bar, and increase the share of events prevented before customer impact. * Partner day to day with the Network Operations Center, Network Engineering, and the Incident Management (Call Leader) program; sit on live HSE/LSE bridges as jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Amazon Business - External Integrations
jobs.jd: Amazon Business System Integrations connects Amazon Business with millions of business users and thousands of partner procurement, ERP, and finance systems. We build the APIs, protocols, and agentic experiences that let customers buy on Amazon Business directly from the systems they already use. As an Applied Scientist on this team, you will own and advance the ML and GenAI capabilities that make these integrations smarter, faster, and more reliable. You will drive model accuracy, scientific innovation, and global scale across external systems integrations. Our work includes API-based and protocol-based shopping, such as punchout and emerging agent protocols, along with agentic interactions where buyers and AI agents search, compare, and purchase through natural language. It also covers partner onboarding and integration automation, mapping and normalizing catalog, product, and order data across many partner formats, and evaluation frameworks that measure the quality, accuracy, and latency of our agents. jobs.jd: As a Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you embed directly with strategic customers to build, optimize, and run custom generative AI models in production alongside their engineering teams. You own complete model workstreams end-to-end from defining the evaluation bar and preparing data, through training and inference optimization, to production deployment. FDE IIs on this team works at the intersection of models and systems. They customize state-of-the-art open-weight and foundation models for new domains, languages, and modalities; migrate and optimize training and inference workloads on AWS Trainium and operate those models as production services. They are autonomous contributors who take on projects where the business goal is clear, but the path is not. They make design trade-offs with appropriate guidance, limit short-term workarounds, coach others on producing high-quality code, and train new team members. Requires up to 25% travel. Customize and post-train models. Adapt open-weight and foundation models to customer domains through continued pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning (including RLHF, RL with verifiable rewards, and multi-turn agentic RL). Build the data pipelines, synthetic data generation, and evaluation harnesses that prove a customized model out performs the baseline on the customer's own quality, latency, and cost bar. Apply these techniques to high-value patterns such as coding agents, domain foundation models, and multi-adapter serving. Build large-scale training and inference systems. Build RL interaction harnesses using NeMo Gym or OpenEnv to connect agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions to training. Develop production inference stacks with engines such as SGLang and vLLM, and optimize throughput, latency, memory footprint, and cost per token through quantization, parallelism, speculative decoding, and batching. jobs.jd: Core to Amazon's DNA is its methodology around executing experiments and prototypes to find the quickest way to prove new ideas, technologies, and business models in a real-world environment. We take emerging technology, including our own inventions, build working prototypes with customers and partners, and demonstrate what becomes possible before the rest of the market gets there. Prototyping is how we do the work. Pushing the technology horizon is why we do it. If you are a highly creative problem solver who works to inspire, motivate, and define innovative solutions; are passionate about technology, understand cloud architectures and platforms, and are quick to pick up emerging technologies; are adept at working with customers to experiment with innovative approaches and validate the technical feasibility of solutions, this could be the role for you. As a Senior Applied Scientist you sit directly with customers and partners. You help them envision complex uses of AWS by building working prototypes of specific use cases, tailored to their data, devices, and systems. Engagements run in short build cycles, typically four to six weeks, and are designed to be innovative and evaluative, demonstrating the art of the possible on AWS while proving a credible path to production. You will work across the areas where we are placing our biggest bets. These shift as the technology does, but today they include: - Physical AI and autonomous robotics. World models, vision-language-action (VLA) models, cloud-based and agentic VLA, real-to-sim and sim-to-real pipelines, and agentic control of physical systems. We challenge the assumption that these models have to live only at the edge. - Autonomous scientific discovery. Multi-agent systems, code agents, and automated research workflows that change how software gets built. - Scaling what we learn. Turning one-off prototypes into reusable patterns and assets the broader field can pick up and run with. You will not just apply these techniques. You will help decide which bets are worth making and prove or disprove them in the open with real customer problems. Key job responsibilities - As a key member of the AWS Specialists and Partner Prototyping team, ensure customer success through hands-on participation producing and demonstrating prototypes on the AWS platform. - Participate in deep architectural and scientific design discussions to ensure prototypes are crafted for successful deployment in the cloud and a credible path to production. - Bring applied science depth to engagements: frame the problem, select and adapt models, design experiments, and judge technical feasibility honestly, including when the answer is that an approach will not work. - Conduct one-to-few and one-to-many training sessions to transfer knowledge to prototyping customers, partners, and internal business partners. - Act as a thought leader for your area of domain expertise across AWS, and share best-practice knowledge among the community. - Author or otherwise contribute to AWS customer-facing publications such as peer reviewed position papers, blogs, and reference patterns. - Act as a technical liaison between customers, service engineering teams, and sales, carrying real-world signal back to the teams building the services. jobs.jd: Do you want to create the greatest-possible worldwide impact in Robotics? Amazon has the world's most exciting treasure trove of robotics challenges. At Amazon Robotics we build high-performance, real-time robotic systems that can perceive, learn, and act intelligently alongside humans—at Amazon scale. Amazon Robotics invents and scales AI systems for robotics in fulfillment. Our mission is to enable robots to interact safely, efficiently, and fluently high density real-world fulfillment centers. Our AI solutions enable robots to learn from their own experiences, from each other, and from humans to build intelligence that feeds itself. We hire and develop subject matter experts in AI with a focus on 3D perception, computer vision, deep learning, and generative modeling. We target high-impact algorithmic unlocks in areas such as 3D scene understanding and completion, semantic occupancy prediction, multi-view 3D reconstruction, depth estimation, shape completion, and real-time inference - all of which have high-value impact for our current and future fulfillment networks. We are seeking an passionate, hands-on, seasoned Senior Applied Scientist who will be deep in code and algorithms; who is technically strong in building scalable 3D perception systems across semantic scene completion, encoder-decoder and transformer architectures (e.g., VoxFormer, MonoScene), voxelized occupancy prediction, panoptic and instance segmentation, depth estimation, point cloud processing, and multi-view fusion. You will drive ideas to products using paradigms such as 3D generative models, query-based transformers, masked autoencoder-style completion, and scalable pseudo-ground-truth data generation. As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will also help lead and mentor our team of applied scientists and engineers. You will take on challenging perception problems - such as completing 3D bin scenes from partial observations, integrating multi-camera inputs, and optimizing inference latency for edge deployment - distill requirements, and then deliver solutions that either leverage existing academic and industrial research or utilize your own out-of-the-box but pragmatic thinking. In addition to coming up with novel solutions and prototypes, you will directly contribute to implementation while you lead. A successful candidate has excellent technical depth in 3D computer vision, scientific vision, project management skills, great communication skills, and a drive to achieve results in a collaborative team environment. You should enjoy the process of solving real-world problems that, quite frankly, haven't been solved at scale anywhere before. Along the way, we guarantee you'll get opportunities to be a disruptor, prolific innovator, and a reputed problem solver—someone who truly enables AI and robotics to significantly impact the lives of millions of consumers. Key job responsibilities Architect, design, and implement 3D perception models - including encoder-decoder networks, query-based transformers, and generative architectures- for semantic occupancy prediction and scene completion on robotic platforms. Own the end-to-end model lifecycle: develop scalable training pipelines, optimize inference latency for ARM-based edge processors, and deploy production models that meet real-time performance targets. Design and scale pseudo-ground-truth data generation pipelines - both heuristic-based and learning-based (e.g., SAM3D, shape completion) to produce curated training samples using SageMaker infrastructure. This is a particularly exciting time to join because we are expanding into new countries, building AI-native capabilities, and beginning to externalize our solutions so that teams beyond our own can benefit from the tools we create. jobs.title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
jobs.jd: About the Team The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Personal AGI organization. Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT. Our recent work includes Beneficial RL https://alignment.openai.com/beneficial-rl/, which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench https://openai.com/index/introducing-mentalhealthbench/, a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations. About the Role We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship. We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required. In this role, you will - Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals. - Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models. - Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings. - Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss. - Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training. - Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute. - Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements. - Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users. You might thrive in this role if you - Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models. - Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit. - Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure. - Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems. - Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous. - Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype. - Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem. jobs.jd: Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video subscriptions such as Apple TV+, HBO Max, Peacock, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads. Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience. As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people. We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you! Key job responsibilities The science challenges include: - Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time. - Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals. - Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles. - Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies. - Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric. A day in the life - Lead the research and development of ML models that personalize advertising decisions for 100M+ customers across 100k+ titles, with production deployment in mind - Develop deep learning architectures (multi-task learning, embedding-based representations) for customer behavior prediction at scale - Design and analyze large-scale A/B experiments, applying causal inference techniques to measure and optimize the impact of ad strategies on customer engagement and monetization - Partner with engineering to ensure models meet production latency and scalability requirements - Collaborate with product managers to frame business problems as tractable ML problems and translate findings into product decisions - Shape the team’s scientific roadmap, identifying high-impact research directions About the team Prime Video Ads is pioneering the use of Generative AI, Deep Learning and Causal ML to empower the next generation of Ads experience in Prime Video. jobs.title: Applied Scientist, Center for Quantum Computing
jobs.jd: Amazon’s Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is building the next generation of quantum computing hardware. The Center for Quantum Computing (CQC) is our longest-horizon bet and operates at the intersection of hardware and physics. The goal is a quantum computer that could solve in hours what today's most robust machines would take thousands of years to compute, unlocking breakthroughs in myriad of areas ranging from advanced materials for batteries to cryptography and fundamentally-secure data sharing protocols. This program involves R&D in device theory, materials science, nano-scale fabrication, superconducting circuit design, cryogenic refrigeration, and quantum algorithms and applications. Currently, the quantum hardware team is focused on improving the underlying chip fabrication of the quantum processor and the scaling of the control system needed to run large-scale quantum circuits. As part of this effort, the team is expanding its chip fabrication capabilities through the construction of a new cleanroom facility dedicated to superconducting quantum chip fabrication, and working with strategic partners to develop scaled versions of the control electronics, I/O wiring, and cryogenic refrigeratation needed for utility-scale quantum computers. We operate with a startup-like pace inside one of the world's most capable technology organizations, combining the urgency of a competitive frontier with the resources and infrastructure of pan Amazon. We are seeking an Applied Scientist III to join our team and drive the design, construction, and operation of quantum processors. You will work alongside world-class physicists and engineers to push the frontier of quantum computing — from laser system design and atom trapping to high-fidelity gate execution and quantum error correction. This is a rare opportunity to be part of shaping a technology that could define the next era of computing. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, and operate quantum computing experiments, including optical trapping arrays, laser cooling and state-preparation systems, and high-fidelity gate-driving optics - Develop and optimize two-qubit entangling gates using interactions, targeting fidelities at or beyond the current state of the art (>99.5%) - Implement and characterize erasure-detection protocols leveraging the metastable-state structure of ¹⁷¹Yb to achieve hardware-native erasure conversion rates >90% - Contribute to quantum error correction experiments, including surface codes and quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, and work toward demonstrating error suppression factors (Λ) well beyond current published records - Design and improve atom-array loading, rearrangement, and continuous replenishment techniques to support registers of thousands to tens of thousands of atoms - Develop control software and calibration routines for high-speed experimental sequences, including real-time feedback and adaptive protocols - Analyze experimental data, build physical models to explain observed behavior, and propose and execute improvements to system performance - Collaborate with theory, software, and hardware engineering teams to co-design quantum architectures, error-correcting codes, and decoder systems - jobs.title: Werkstudent Fulfillment
jobs.jd: Ben jij een HBO- of WO-student in een bedrijfseconomische en/of logistieke richting en wil je naast je studie relevante werkervaring opdoen? Bij Priva krijg je de kans om mee te werken aan verschillende projecten binnen een innovatieve en internationale organisatie. Wat ga je doen? Als werkstudent binnen Fulfilment ondersteun je verschillende teams en werk je mee aan projecten. Je gaat de ene keer aan de slag binnen één specifieke afdeling , en de andere keer ga je meewerken aan projecten die meerdere afdelingen raken. Fulfilment bestaat uit de afdelingen Production, Logistics & Warehousing, Supplier Quality Engineering en Procurement & Planning. Afhankelijk van het project houd je je onder andere bezig met: Ondersteunen van collega's bij operationele en administratieve werkzaamheden; Meewerken aan lopende projecten binnen de verschillende Fulfilment-afdelingen; Verzamelen, analyseren en verwerken van data; Signaleren van verbetermogelijkheden en meedenken over efficiëntere processen; Zelfstandig oppakken en uitvoeren van (LEAN-)deelprojecten. Zo doe je naast je studie waardevolle praktijkervaring op en krijg je de mogelijkheid om jouw kennis direct toe te passen binnen een professionele werkomgeving. Wie zijn wij? Wij zijn Priva! Priva is een familiebedrijf, gevestigd in het Westland. Het is de missie van Priva om een optimale omgeving te creëren waarin zowel planten als mensen kunnen werken, groeien en zich ontwikkelen. Wij bieden wereldwijde oplossingen voor de tuinbouw, gebouwautomatisering en alles daartussenin. Wij zijn toonaangevend in de ontwikkeling en productie van technologie voor het optimaliseren van omgevingsomstandigheden en processen. Onze ambitie is om bekend te staan als de toonaangevende technologie- en dienstverlener voor duurzame stedelijke delta's. We zijn er trots op dat onze oplossingen resulteren in een lager verbruik van natuurlijke hulpbronnen, zoals energie en water. Om onze missie en ambitie waar te maken, zijn we op zoek naar toegewijde collega's. We zijn er trots op dat we met ruim 500 collega's, in 16 internationale vestigingen verdeeld over 12 landen samen met meer dan 400 internationale installatiepartners werken aan het leveren van onze duurzame oplossingen en diensten in meer dan 100 landen. Wie ben jij? Wij zoeken een enthousiaste student die graag kennismaakt met de praktijk en initiatief durft te nemen. Daarnaast: Volg je een HBO- of WO-opleiding in een bedrijfseconomische en/of logistieke richting; Ben je 16 tot 24 uur per week beschikbaar, in overleg; Werk je analytisch en nauwkeurig; Beschik je over goede communicatieve vaardigheden; Heb je een proactieve en zelfstandige werkhouding; Beheers je zowel de Nederlandse als Engelse taal goed, mondeling en schriftelijk. Wat je krijgt? Naast een interessante bijbaan waarin je relevante werkervaring opdoet, bieden we je: Een uitdagende werkplek waarin je jezelf kunt ontwikkelen en waardevolle praktijkervaring opdoet. Een passend en marktconform salaris Bedrijfsrestaurant tegen betaalbare prijzen, gratis fruit en lekkere koffie in The Hub. Een actieve personeelsvereniging & vitaliteitsteam met PrivaFit! Workshops waaraan je deel kan nemen. Toegang tot onze gratis fitnessfaciliteiten op locatie, waar je kunt meedoen aan Crossfit-, Pilates-, Yoga- en Full Body Workout of speel een potje tafelvoetbal en tafeltennis mee. Solliciteren Wil jij naast je studie relevante werkervaring opdoen en ontdekken hoe het is om binnen Priva Fulfilment aan verschillende projecten te werken? Solliciteer dan direct! jobs.title: Data Scientist – Automation and Ecological Data Analysis (5165)
jobs.jd: Bennett Aerospace Inc., a subsidiary of Three Saints Bay, LLC , and a Federal Government Contractor industry leader, isseeking a highly motivateda Data Scientist to develop automation frameworks and analytical models that accelerate the interpretation of ecological field data within the Hydrogeomorphic (HGM) approach. The successful candidate will design, test, and implement algorithms that streamline functional assessments and ensure consistent outputs across geographic regions and mission areas. Position Responsibilities Develop algorithms and automated workflows to process field-collected ecological data. Build data pipelines and scripts in R, Python, or equivalent tools to support reproducible analysis. Ensure automation tools generate consistent, defensible outputs for wetland functional assessments. Conduct verification and validation using test datasets and iterative refinement. Deliver technical documentation, user guides, and reports to support tool deployment and peer review. Position Requirements: Master’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, or related field (PhD preferred). 5–10 years of experience in data analysis, modeling, and automation workflows. Proficiency in R, Python, and statistical modeling techniques. Experience working with ecological, environmental, or engineering datasets preferred. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with proven ability to translate complex data into decision-support products. Security Requirements: Must be a US Citizen with the ability to obtain a US Government Clearance if required. Background check Applicants selected will be subject to a Government background investigation and must meet eligibility and suitability requirements. Must be a US Citizen with the ability to obtain a US Government security clearance. Successful Pass of Bennett Aerospace Background Investigation, Drug Screening and Credit Check Apply online here at: This position is remote, potential for hybrid work at the University of Montana The salary range for this position is $87,000 - $97,000 VEVRAA Federal Contractor Three Saints Bay, LLC and its subsidiaries offer a team-oriented working environment and the opportunity to work with exceptional, dedicated industry professionals. We offer our employees a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to take part in exciting projects with government and commercial clients, both domestic and international. jobs.title: Robotics Applied Scientist
jobs.jd: Amazon is seeking exceptional talent to help develop the next generation of advanced robotics systems that will transform automation at Amazon's scale. We're building robotic systems that combine frontier AI, sophisticated control, and advanced mechanical design to create adaptable automation capable of working safely alongside humans in dynamic environments. This is an opportunity to shape the future of robotics and automation at an unprecedented scale, working with world-class teams pushing the boundaries of what's possible in robotic manipulation, locomotion, and human-robot interaction. We are seeking an Applied Scientist to develop tactile- and force-driven manipulation policies for highly dexterous, multi-fingered robotic hands and grippers. In this role you will research and build policy learning algorithms that enable robotic hands to perform grasping and in-hand manipulation in unstructured, real-world environments, using touch and force feedback as first-class signals rather than afterthoughts. Much of this work is grounded in reinforcement learning. To be successful you need to be highly motivated, dive deep, and deliver to the highest standards. You will demonstrate strong working knowledge of modern policy learning methods, with expertise in taking algorithms from simulation onto real hardware. That means being comfortable working against real physical constraints and treating sim-to-real as a core research problem rather than optimizing for benchmark numbers alone. You will work across tactile signal processing, contact-rich manipulation, sim-to-real transfer, and multi-modal sensor fusion to build robust solutions for autonomous grasping, dexterous re-orientation, and fine motor control. You will bring the desire to learn from new challenges, and the problem-solving and communication skills to work within a highly interactive and experienced team. Key job responsibilities - Design and train manipulation policies that leverage tactile and force feedback for dexterous grasping, in-hand manipulation, and contact-rich tasks, using reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or hybrid approaches. - Drive sim-to-real transfer, closing the gap between simulated and physical performance on real robotic hands. - Shape objectives and control strategies with the hardware in mind, accounting for how motors and actuators actually behave: transmission ratios, torque versus power, backdrivability, and thermal limits. - Build simulation-based and on-robot evaluation frameworks, with benchmarks and metrics that make tactile perception and policy performance systematically comparable across iterations. - Own scientific and technical projects within the tactile sensing and manipulation workstreams, driving from research concept through deployment on physical robotic systems — and, at the senior level, set direction across a workstream. - Collaborate with hardware, mechanical design, firmware, and controls teams — and with partner applied science organizations — to translate research advances into deployable robotic capabilities, and to inform sensor and actuator design decisions with policy-level requirements. - Publish at top-tier venues and build collaborations with the external research community. - Contribute to a strong scientific bar on the team through code and design review, and mentor engineers and interns working on real-world manipulation and sensing problems. A day in the life Your morning might start with a standup alongside hardware and controls engineers reviewing overnight sim-to-real training runs on a multi-finger gripper, debugging why a grasp policy that worked in simulation is slipping on a real sensor array. Mid-morning you join the weekly tactile sensing workstream to align on sensor integration milestones and share early results from a contact-state estimator you have been prototyping. After lunch you spend a focused block iterating on a reinforcement learning reward formulation, testing variations in simulation before queuing runs on the cluster. Later you pair with a mechanical engineer to review sensor placement trade-offs on an upcoming gripper revision, then wrap the day by drafting a short experiment write-up and sketching next steps for a conference submission. No two days look exactly the same: one week you may be collecting teleoperated demonstrations on the physical robot to seed an imitation learning pipeline; the next you could be deep in a codebase refactor to support a new tactile modality. Throughout, you balance hands-on research — writing algorithms, running experiments, analyzing data — with cross-team collaboration and mentoring. The common thread is moving from research insight to working capability on real hardware, with a tight feedback loop between simulation and the physical world. About the team Our is developing next-generation manipulation capabilities for highly dexterous multi-fingered grippers and hands. Our work spans tactile sensor development, manipulation policy learning, and the tight integration of sensing hardware with intelligent control software. We are building systems that can feel, adapt, and manipulate with human-level dexterity. You will join a team working at the frontier of tactile sensing and contact-rich manipulation, helping define how robots perceive and interact with objects through touch. Because we build the hands as well as the policies that drive them, you will have a direct line to the sensor, actuator, and mechanism designs your algorithms depend on — and real influence over how they evolve. This is an opportunity to solve hard problems across perception, learning, and physical interaction alongside a team of scientists and engineers building toward real-world deployment. - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Research or applied experience in one or more of: tactile sensing, manipulation policy learning, contact-rich manipulation, dexterous grasping, or multi-modal perception for ro
